findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: It was observed that no employees present during today’s inspection had completed a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) course. A CFM should be present at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM is able to oversee proper employee hygiene, food handling practices, safe holding temperatures, and overall reduces the risk of food-borne illness. Ensure a CFM is present on staff during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.[C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate the faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. Be sure to educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. After washing hands, make sure to use a barrier to operate faucet handles to prevent contaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris on the following food contact surfaces:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Biofilm at several soda nozzles at the drink station directly south of the car.. CORRECTED- staff removed the nozzles to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the three part sink.
2) Biofilm at the soda gun holder on the North side of the bar. CORRECTED- the space was wiped with a sanitizer cloth. 
Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The gasket of the kitchen salad prep cooler was observed to be loose. This loose gasket may affect the ability of the unit to cold hold, and may act as a potential food contaminant. Replace or repair the gasket by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.  [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer bucket available along the cook-line at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure making a sanitizer bucket is a part of opening procedures, so that food contact surfaces may be frequently sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine in the bar area tested at 0ppm (Cl). The machine was tested on several occasions with the facility’s and the inspector’s test strips. PIC contacted an EcoLab technician to service the machine. The facility is instructed to use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine can be serviced. Be sure that dish machines are testing at the manufacturer's recommended concentration to ensure that dishes are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels available at the kitchen handwashing sink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Upon request, staff refilled the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

[P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods were observed out of temperature in the short cookline prep cooler. Foods were observed as follows (probed): shredded chicken at 61F and 47F; shredded cheese at 46F; lettuce at 50F; pico at 46F; sliced tomatoes at 48F; hardboiled eggs at 49F; bleu cheese at 59F; mac & cheese at 46F; lettuce at 45F; sour cream at 48F; and ranch at 47F. CORRECTED- All out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Several foods (salsa, lettuce, sour cream, and southwest ranch) were 45F or below and were moved to a functioning cooler.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The short cookline prep cooler is not holding foods at 41F or below. Foods were found 44-61F (probed), and were voluntarily discarded. PIC called for maintenance/repairs. A tech is expected to be on site later today. Ensure all cold holding units are functioning sufficiently to hold foods at 41F or below.
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
An employee jacket was observed under the wait station counter, amongst single service articles and other supplies used for service. CORRECTED- PIC moved the jacket to the designated employee storage area. Ensure employees store their clothing and other belongings away from food/single service items/etc that are used for service.
6-501.110: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]
